newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's spring grain sowing near year-ago level.
newsitem.headline: Russia's spring grain sowing near year-ago level.

text.p: Russia's State Statistics Committee said on Monday it would not publish recent figures for the spring grain sowing campaign, but an agriculture official said plantings were only slightly behind year-ago levels.

Ivan Gridasov, head of the Agriculture Ministry's crop sowing section, was quoted by Interfax news agency as saying spring grains and pulses (not including maize) had been sown to 27.3 million hectares as of May 24 -- 492,000 ha, or 1.8 percent, below year-ago levels.
The total area sown to all spring crops was 39.2 million ha, he said, but he gave no comprehensive comparison figure.
A committee spokesman said the body had decided not to publish the data due to the nature of the information, but she gave no details. The committee usually publishes the data.
Gridasov was quoted as saying equipment shortages had delayed sowing and that fuel supplies for tractors were one third of required levels.
Russia sowed a total of 53.8 million ha to all crops last year, including 40 million ha to spring crops of all kinds.
Andrei Sizov of agricultural consultancy SovEcon Ltd has said the area sown to spring wheat may set a new record and reach 17.4 million ha this year, up from 16.4 million in 1996.
He said on Monday there were no indications Russia's 1996 sowing campaign was in trouble and that the government's forecast of a 70 million tonne net harvest was realistic.
